4	The multi-channel degradation model (\S\ref{sec:results}) raises an interventional question: if confusability drives type confusion, can we decompose the schema so that confusable types never co-occur in the same prompt?  We test this idea with \textbf{Schema-DAG-Guided Decomposition} (SDGD), a method that uses the pairwise SCS matrix to partition types into low-confusability batches, runs extraction independently on each batch, and merges the results.
5	
6	\paragraph{Decomposition protocol.}
7	We compute hierarchical clustering over the SCS matrix and cut the dendrogram so that highly similar types fall into separate batches. Each batch is presented to the LLM as an independent extraction prompt; predictions are then merged via set union. We compare four modes: (i)~\textbf{single\_pass}, the undecomposed baseline; (ii)~\textbf{sdgd\_zero}, SCS-guided partitioning; (iii)~\textbf{random\_batch}, random partitioning with matched batch sizes; and (iv)~\textbf{per\_type}, the extreme case where each type is extracted in isolation, following the strategy of \citet{uniner-2024}. Table~\ref{tab:sdgd_results} summarizes the results on Few-NERD.

4	Training-free LLM information extraction---prompting a large language model with a target schema and asking it to extract structured information without any task-specific fine-tuning---enables rapid deployment across new domains and ontologies. Approaches span instruction tuning for unified IE \cite{instructuie-2023}, code-style schema encoding \cite{knowcoder-2024,codeie-2023}, annotation-guided zero-shot extraction \cite{gollie-2024,adelie-2024}, and schema-driven decoding \cite{slot-2025,oneke-2025}. These methods perform well with moderate schemas (4--20 types) but none investigates how performance degrades as schema complexity scales. Our work fills this gap.

Recent surveys categorize LLM-based IE along instruction-tuning and code-generation axes \cite{llm4ie-survey-2024}. Approaches span instruction tuning for unified IE \cite{instructuie-2023}, code-style schema encoding \cite{knowcoder-2024,codeie-2023}, annotation-guided zero-shot extraction \cite{gollie-2024,adelie-2024}, and schema-driven decoding \cite{slot-2025,oneke-2025}. For NER, \citet{xie-zeroshot-ner-2023} decompose zero-shot NER by entity type to improve ChatGPT performance, \citet{promptner-2023} leverage entity type definitions for prompt-based extraction, and further methods include ChatGPT distillation \cite{uniner-2024}, bidirectional transformers \cite{gliner-2024,gliner2-2025}, self-improvement \cite{self-improve-ner-2024}, type descriptions \cite{zeroner-2025}, and guided synthesis \cite{guidex-2025,nuner-2024}. Relation extraction benefits from self-prompting \cite{self-prompting-re-2024} and retrieval-augmented code generation \cite{code4uie-2024}. \citet{familiarity-2025} highlight evaluation pitfalls by quantifying label shifts in zero-shot NER. Orthogonally, constrained decoding via JSON schema enforcement \cite{json-schema-bench-2025} is increasingly adopted to guarantee structurally valid extraction outputs; all our experiments use vLLM's constrained JSON decoding (\S\ref{sec:model}).

These methods perform well with moderate schemas (4--20 types) but none investigates how performance degrades as schema complexity scales, nor proposes quantitative metrics for inter-type confusability. Our work fills both gaps.
